title: bug: both launchers export MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE into the agent CLI's environment, so any process the CLI spawns (a test, a helper, a fixture run) can append to the seat's live launch receipt; scope the variable to the wrapper's own usage writes (wrapper-side twin of task-03418dc2, both launchers)
description:
Hunt #18 (task-1c736204) held this item back until the open launcher rows land.

Problem: task-03418dc2 found that prompt-cache.test.mjs, prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs and onboarding.mjs run the usage stream helper with the seat's inherited MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE. Their fixture codex/claude usage therefore went into 48 live launch receipts: 248 fake rows charged to 28 tasks between 10-24 and 11-03, and usage-report shows codex usage in Claude-only launches. 03418dc2 fixes the test side. The root exposure is in the launchers: they export MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE into the environment the agent CLI inherits, at scripts/moe-agent.sh :884/:891 and moe-agent.ps1 :1251-1252 (line numbers at 3cd256eb). So any child of the CLI can write to the live receipt.

Fix direction: only the wrapper's own usage writes should see the receipt path. Either pass the path explicitly to the wrapper's helper calls and unset it in the CLI's environment, or clear it for the CLI launch alone. Keep the parity-check twins in step (codes, env names), and keep the receipt that the wrapper's own usage-session/usage-receipt calls produce byte-for-byte unchanged.

Sequencing: this row depends on 3416b309 (both launchers, in REVIEW) and 62ec51f1 (moe-agent.ps1, WORKING), which hold the same files. d861f3de, the third row the hunter named, is already DONE. Re-anchor every line number on the landed launchers.

Note: the 48 polluted historical receipts under logs/moe-usage stay as they are, by the governor's decision (#governors msg-3c3dd428). Rewriting logs loses provenance, so usage-report totals for 10-24 to 11-03 include about 248 fixture rows.
definitionOfDone: Under both launchers, the agent CLI's environment no longer carries MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE. A launcher test pins it for each twin: a child of the CLI sees it unset, while the wrapper's own usage writes still reach the receipt.
The receipt that one launch's own usage calls produce is unchanged, shown by a before/after run of the same launch in the postflight harness. parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 pass.
The verification quotes the harness results for both twins, and bash -n plus the PowerShell parser check pass on the edited launchers.

implementationPlan.description:
moe-agent.sh: keep the usage receipt pair out of every exported environment and hand it only to the wrapper's own usage helper calls (lines at 500e3f29; re-anchor by text if bbd7ad2d/1dfec7a4/6b3ab9d8 or 62ec51f1's rework moved them).
(a) start_moe_usage_receipt() (:869-895) exports nothing. Its first line becomes `unset MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE USAGE_RECEIPT_CONTEXT` (this also drops an inherited export). Add `supplied=""` to the existing `local` list and build the python context with `if ! supplied=$(...)`, so the test still sees the substitution's status. usage-session.mjs gets it as a one-command prefix: `prepared=$(MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON="$supplied" "$NODE_CMD" "$SCRIPT_DIR/usage-session.mjs" "$PROJECT" 2>/dev/null) || prepared=""`. Delete `export MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON` and the two `unset MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON` in the failure branches. Error handling stays fail-open: both failure branches still print `[usage] MOE_USAGE_REPORT_UNAVAILABLE` and `return 0`. On success, set the UNEXPORTED shell variables `USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE="$receipt_file" USAGE_RECEIPT_CONTEXT="$receipt_context"`, then run `MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE="$USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE" MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON="$USAGE_RECEIPT_CONTEXT" "$NODE_CMD" "$PROMPT_CACHE_HELPER" usage-start "$provider" >/dev/null || true`.
(b) Each stream helper gets the same pair as an inline per-command prefix, `MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE="${USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE:-}" MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON="${USAGE_RECEIPT_CONTEXT:-}"`, placed directly before `"$NODE_CMD" "$PROMPT_CACHE_HELPER"` in: the codex exec pipeline (:11408, after the existing MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE..MOE_SERENA_PROJECT_ROOT prefixes); and both claude print pipelines (:12044 and :12057, the `| "$NODE_CMD" "$PROMPT_CACHE_HELPER" claude-stream |` element). Do NOT add a shell function for this: prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs runs the codex pipeline line alone (`            agent_git_exec "$COMMAND_BIN" "${COMMAND_ARGV[@]}" \` -> `            set -e`), so a new function would be undefined there. An empty value acts like today's unset for the writer (usage-receipt.mjs:79 `if (!file) return`; readContext('') -> {}), so the rows stay byte-identical.
(c) The main-loop top (:9921-9922) keeps its comment; its unset line also names USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE USAGE_RECEIPT_CONTEXT.
(d) A comment above start_moe_usage_receipt() says why. task-03418dc2 found fixture usage from processes the CLI starts in 48 live receipts. So no agent CLI, nothing the CLI starts, and no other wrapper child (the post-flight quality gate included) may see the pair. Name the twin, Invoke-MoeUsageHelper in moe-agent.ps1. Extend the codex block's 'The helper alone gets the TOOL-witness env' comment so it also names the receipt pair.
Keep these test anchors byte-identical: `start_moe_usage_receipt() {`, `# End usage receipt helpers.`, `        LAUNCH_SKIPPED=false`, `            start_moe_usage_receipt codex headless`, `            agent_git_exec "$COMMAND_BIN" "${COMMAND_ARGV[@]}" \`, `            set -e`. Keep the main-loop `{ ... exit }` group, and `bash -n` must pass. Edit only with the Edit tool, in W (mem:gotcha-wrapper-slice-tests-execute-text).

implementationPlan.description:
moe-agent.ps1 twin: keep the pair in script scope, and set it in `$env:` only around the wrapper's own helper calls. A native process copies the environment when it starts, so the CLI, the heartbeat job and every later child never see it (lines at 500e3f29; re-anchor by text).
(a) Start-MoeUsageReceipt (:1235-1261). On entry, clear `$env:MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE`, `$env:MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON`, `$script:MoeUsageReceiptFile` and `$script:MoeUsageContextJson`. `$env:MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON` holds the supplied @{...} JSON only for the usage-session.mjs call. On success, set `$script:MoeUsageReceiptFile = [string]$usageSession.file` and `$script:MoeUsageContextJson = $usageSession.context | ConvertTo-Json -Compress` (exactly today's values), then run usage-start through Invoke-MoeUsageHelper. The catch clears both script variables and keeps `Write-Warning 'MOE_USAGE_REPORT_UNAVAILABLE'`, so error handling stays fail-open. The finally clears both `$env:` names, then restores `$global:LASTEXITCODE` as today.
(b) Add `function Invoke-MoeUsageHelper([scriptblock]$Call)` after Start-MoeUsageReceipt and before `# End usage receipt helpers.` (usage-launcher.test.mjs runs that block as its preamble). It sets both `$env:` names from the script variables, runs `& $Call`, and clears both in `finally`. Add a comment giving the why and the twin (the sh helper calls' MOE_USAGE_* prefixes).
(c) In the `$parseStreamJson` "result" branch (:11449), wrap the existing `$line | & node $promptCacheHelper claude-stream | Select-Object -Skip 1 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }` in `Invoke-MoeUsageHelper { ... }`. The scriptblock reads `$line` and `$promptCacheHelper` through dynamic scope.
(d) In the claude launch `finally` (:11493), test `$script:MoeUsageReceiptFile` instead of `$env:MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE`. Run the `'' | & node $promptCacheHelper claude-stream | Out-Null` fallback through Invoke-MoeUsageHelper, inside the existing try/catch.
(e) In the codex exec `ForEach-Object -Begin` (:10885-10901), after the TOOL-witness lines, add `if ($script:MoeUsageReceiptFile) { $psi.EnvironmentVariables['MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE'] = $script:MoeUsageReceiptFile; $psi.EnvironmentVariables['MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON'] = $script:MoeUsageContextJson }`. Put no `else` anywhere in this block: two tests cut it at the first `            } else {` after the codex exec line, and a deeper-indented one matches too.
(f) At the main-loop top (:9699-9701), also reset both script variables to `$null`.
Keep byte-identical: `function Start-MoeUsageReceipt`, `# End usage receipt helpers.`, `            $parseStreamJson = {`, `            # Usage receipt launch boundary.`, `                Start-MoeUsageReceipt 'codex' 'headless'`, the codex `                & {` line and its `Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand @CommandArgs @codexSeatArgs @codexExecOverrides exec --json -C "$script:cliRoot" @codexSandboxArgs "$shortPrompt"` line, and the `Remove-MoeAgentGitGuard` tail. Add no new MOE_* code or env name (parity). Keep the UTF-8 BOM, and ParseFile must report 0 errors.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/tests/usage-launcher.test.mjs: pin the scope for each twin. Engines are /bin/bash under Linux node, and powershell.exe, pwsh.exe and Git Bash under Windows node. Write the test first and prove it RED (below).
(a) Add a fake-provider prelude. It writes `<MOE_TEST_DIR>/cli-env.json` = `{receipt: process.env.MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE ?? null, context: process.env.MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON ?? null}`. Then it runs a CHILD, `spawnSync(process.execPath, [path.join(process.env.MOE_TEST_SCRIPTS, 'prompt-cache.mjs'), 'usage-start', '<provider>'], {stdio: 'ignore'})`. That child is the task-03418dc2 path: a fixture usage helper appending to whatever receipt it inherits. Prepend the prelude to the fake sources of 'real Claude launch' and 'real Codex launch' (both withResult arms). Assert cli-env.json is `{receipt: null, context: null}`. The existing `receipts.length === 2` assertion (pending + reported/missing, one launchId) then proves both halves: the child appended nothing, and the wrapper's own writes still landed.
(b) Add a new per-engine test, 'interactive Claude launch keeps the receipt from the CLI and its child'. It uses the claude cut with no print args (sh `PRINT_ARGS=()`, ps1 `$usePrintMode=$false` and `$printArgs=@()`), the same prelude, and exitCode 23. Assert CHILD_EXIT=23, cli-env.json both null, and exactly one receipt row, with coverage 'pending' and launchMode 'interactive'.
(c) In 'usage metadata is fresh for each task and resume', after the first start, print what a child of the wrapper would inherit and assert both values are empty. ps1: `$env:MOE_USAGE_RECEIPT_FILE` and `$env:MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON`. sh: a single-quoted `"$NODE_CMD" -e` probe printing both. This pins that the post-flight gate and every other wrapper child inherit nothing.
Keep run(), between(), guard() and every anchor unchanged. RED proof: a scratch copy holding the base launchers (`git show <base>:scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}`) fails (a)-(c) on every engine, because cli-env.json carries the receipt path and the receipt has 3 rows. Quote that in complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Unset the pair only in the CLI launch funnel (sh agent_git_exec, ps1 Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand). Rejected. ps1 parses the claude result line while the CLI is still running, so clearing the process env for the CLI's lifetime would blank the claude-stream helper's receipt. In sh the pair would stay exported for the post-flight quality gate and every other wrapper child, and a gate running Moe's usage tests would pollute the receipt exactly as the CLI's child does.
2. Pass the receipt path on helper argv (--receipt-file). Rejected. It changes the prompt-cache.mjs and usage-session.mjs CLI contracts and their tests, and usage-session.mjs deliberately takes its JSON context through env so PS 5.1 never round-trips JSON quotes through native argv.
3. Chosen: unexported shell or script-scope storage, plus per-call env for the wrapper's own helpers. It is symmetric across the twins, covers the CLI, its children and every other wrapper child, and keeps helper inputs identical.
MOE_USAGE_CONTEXT_JSON is scoped too. Only the writer and usage-session use it, nothing in the CLI subtree reads it, and both names are always set and cleared together.
Where to show DoD 2: a new arm in postflight.{sh,ps1} was rejected for size. postflight-vm-route's T-legacy already runs one full-wrapper claude headless launch in a fresh project, with a fake CLI that records its env, and both twins run from postflight.{sh,ps1}. That keeps the plan at 5 files (no 6-file heavy floor).
No docs change. No doc names these variables as visible to the CLI, and the receipt format is unchanged.
